themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 65 this week compared to a 16.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 285% increase (z-score: 4.11)—suggesting a new or concentrated source of disruption in East Flatbush.
evidence: 65 noise-street/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 16.9 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
285% spike with z-score of 4.11, indicating statistical significance
No corresponding spike in residential noise, suggesting localized source (construction, venue, vendor activity)
reporting_angles: Door-knock reporting: which blocks are hotspots? Interview affected residents on specific complaints (hours, type of noise)
Track the source: construction sites, food vendors, transit hub activity, or special event? Cross-reference with DOB permits (310 filings recent) and NYPD incident data

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping & Dumpster Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints reached 23 last week (142% above the 9.5-complaint weekly average), while dumpster complaints hit 4 (700% above 0.5 average)—a converging environmental sanitation crisis emerging over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: Illegal dumping: 23 complaints last week vs. 9.5 weekly average (142% spike, z-score: 4.02)
Dumpster complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 7.0)
Combined signal suggests either coordinated illegal dumping activity or breakdown in waste management enforcement
reporting_angles: Map the dumping hotspots using 311 complaint geocoding; interview DSNY about enforcement gaps and resource allocation
Investigate: is this tied to nearby development activity (79 new building permits filed recently) or organized waste diversion?

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Alert
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints exploded to 3 two weeks ago from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)—indicating a potential localized contamination or supply issue affecting a subset of East Flatbush.
evidence: Water quality complaints: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69—highest on list)
This spike predates the water leak (537 total over 90 days) and plumbing complaints (826 total), suggesting quality, not volume
Status unknown on whether complaints have subsided or persist
reporting_angles: Contact DEP immediately: has a boil water notice been issued? Request water testing data and complaint location maps
Interview affected residents: discoloration, taste, odor, illness? Cross-check complaint addresses for geographic pattern (single building, block, or district-wide)

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Root Issues
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked 700% (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 average, z-score: 5.42), while root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints jumped 182% (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 average)—a converging infrastructure threat linked to street trees.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Root/sewer/sidewalk condition: 6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average (182% spike, z-score: 3.68)
Convergence suggests either storm damage, contractor activity, or systematic tree removal/neglect triggering foundation/sidewalk complaints
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department: have there been recent tree removal requests, disease outbreaks, or storm damage in East Flatbush?
Canvas affected blocks: are trees being cut without permits, or is root damage causing sidewalk/sewer failures? Tie to DOB alteration/demolition permits

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Concern
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked 433% (4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average, z-score: 3.92), a significant but not-yet-clarified environmental signal that warrants investigation into possible emissions sources or pollution events.
evidence: Air quality complaints: 4 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 3.92)
Timing (3 weeks ago) makes this slightly older than other urgent spikes, but still anomalous
No follow-up complaints in recent data suggest issue may have resolved or been temporary
reporting_angles: Check EPA AirNow data and NYC DEP air quality monitors for East Flatbush during the 3-week-ago window—was there a measurable event?
Interview complainants if locatable: odor, visibility, respiratory impact? Link to construction/industrial activity (recent permits, Constellation CB 17 rezoning)
